title: Deployment Strategy Decision Matrix
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Software Architecture
description: Set your needs for zero downtime, rollback speed, low cost, and live-traffic validation, then see which deployment strategy (blue-green, canary, rolling update, or recreate) has the smallest gap, what tradeoff it accepts, and how its release unfolds phase by phase.

educational.topic: Blue-green, canary, rolling, and recreate deployment strategies
learningObjectives: Students will be able to select the most appropriate deployment strategy for a given set of quality attribute priorities (rollback speed, zero-downtime requirement, cost tolerance, traffic validation need) and justify the selection with tradeoff analysis.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Commit-then-compare evaluation with a transparent gap model and a stepped process walk-through
keyQuestions: Which of your stated needs does each strategy fail to meet, and by how much?
What does the recommended strategy cost you that the runner-up would not?
During the release, how long do two versions serve users at the same time, and what does that require of the data schema?
commonMisconceptions: Zero-downtime strategies are interchangeable (they differ in rollback speed, cost, and how much real traffic validates the release).
A rolling update is a canary release (its traffic share is a side effect of the instance count, not a controlled, monitored experiment).
Blue-green is always the safest choice (it validates nothing with live traffic before all users switch).
assessmentOpportunities: Give a deployability scenario (for example, "a defective release must be reverted within one minute with no failed customer requests") and ask students to choose a strategy, name the tradeoff accepted, and classify the decision as a risk or a non-risk for that scenario.
